builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Kaer: Security-Aware Replanning for Multi-Agent Systems
summary: Kaer replaces direct exposure of raw agent feedback to the orchestrator during replanning with abstract diagnostic templates, a fixed set of deterministic repair operators, and mandatory policy checks on revised plans, substituting for per-tool access control and static pre-execution enforcement that leave the replanning phase unguarded. The cost is a constrained replanning vocabulary that slightly reduces task completion on tasks whose failures do not fit the predefined templates, plus engineering effort to define templates, operators, and policies. It can fail when a legitimate failure mode falls outside the template set (blocking necessary recovery) or when the deterministic operators cannot express the required plan repair, leaving the system secure but stuck.
rationale: A small team running orchestrated agents can adopt the underlying design pattern (templated feedback, restricted repair operators, policy-checked plan revisions) at negligible infrastructure cost, but should validate the utility trade-off on their own tasks since abstract templates degrade completion on some workloads.
technique: Security-aware replanning via templated feedback and repair operators

claims.statement: Kaer replaces direct exposure of raw agent feedback to the orchestrator during replanning with abstract diagnostic templates, a fixed set of deterministic repair operators, and mandatory policy checks on revised plans, substituting for per-tool access control and static pre-execution enforcement that leave the replanning phase unguarded. The cost is a constrained replanning vocabulary that slightly reduces task completion on tasks whose failures do not fit the predefined templates, plus engineering effort to define templates, operators, and policies. It can fail when a legitimate failure mode falls outside the template set (blocking necessary recovery) or when the deterministic operators cannot express the required plan repair, leaving the system secure but stuck.

On the Cintra benchmark, Kaer achieves higher robustness to replanning exploits than undefended Magentic-One and the ControlValve defense, with task-completion utility comparable to ControlValve; no quantitative factor is reported in the abstract.
